analysis.title: US Energy: Megawatts, Molecules & Minerals: Guns & Butter Redux
key_insights: Last week saw volatility across equities, bonds, commodities and FX. Momentum had its largest single-day advance in five years on Thursday (5.7 standard deviations) but still closed down 7.5% on the week. The author calls the bounce a dead-cat bounce.

The 30-year Treasury yield rose 11bps on the Fed decision day, the largest rise on a Fed decision day in 15 years. The author reads this as the market saying rolling energy supply disruptions, together with a hot real economy, are structural rather than transitory.

The author argues the 'Fed put' has flipped from a rate cut to a rate hike in an environment of abundant aggregate demand and rolling energy supply shocks. In the market's eyes the Fed failed to deliver that put at the FOMC.

2Q26 earnings calls across power, steel, copper, refined products and energy cite strong demand (MTZ, NXT, BE, GEV, NUE, STLD, FCX, DINO, CVX). Hyperscaler capex budgets rose from already high levels and some showed improving ROIC.

Demand confirmation did not rescue momentum or power stocks. The argument is that the problem is the discount rate: with the Fed soft on inflation while demand booms, long yields rise and multiples compress, as in 2022.

The author draws an analog to the mid-to-late 1960s 'Guns & Butter' period. GDP growth was above 6%, inflation below 2% and unemployment 4.5% and falling at the start. Inflation rose to above 6% by the end, yields surged and the S&P 500 forward multiple fell from near 19x in 1965 to near 15x two years later.

Parallels drawn to today: Vietnam War buildout maps to Iran, Great Society fiscal expansion maps to OBBBA, and the 'nifty fifty' emerged then as AI/power names have now. The 10-year yield started both 1965 and 2026 at about 4.2%, and in the 1960s it doubled to about 8% by the end of the decade.

Resource equities did not outperform in the 1960s because of price controls: Texas Railroad Commission prorationing and import quotas on crude, regulated natural gas, gold pegged at $35, and copper at a government-administered price about half the LME quote. The author says 2026 is 1965 without those commodity price controls, so inflation has a right-tail risk.

The author concludes he wants to be long resource equities, wants to revisit the 'HALO' playbook, and questions whether current Energy and Materials weights in the S&P 500 are right. Energy is compared with Mag7 on forward free cash flow estimates.

Midstream earnings week: possible guidance raises at LNG, ET, SUN, WES, TRGP. Updates expected from WMB (6+ GW behind-the-meter backlog, Transco expansions), PAA (2026 capex raise) and KGS (power generation additions). SOBO faces a regulatory setback on its Bridger pipeline as Montana's environmental agency rescinded a waiver.

Midstream positioning per sales: WMB may be the most crowded long in midstream with a tricky setup. OKE is again the most crowded short. ET is a consensus long. PAA is a short moving toward neutral. TRGP is liked by all. KGS is a crowded long. LNG crowding has cleaned up.
IPP positioning: sentiment has improved. VST and TLN are the most crowded, relatively. CEG is the funding short because of its mix similarity to VST. No big contracting updates are expected on calls.

E&P positioning: FANG is a modest net long, upbeat print expected, and JPM's Arun Jayaram sees a possible power project FID in 2026 or early 2027. DVN is a fairly crowded long with low expectations. OXY is one of the more crowded longs and may lay out a medium-term growth outlook through 2029. COP is a short for hedge funds because catalysts are far out. EOG is no longer a consensus short but remains a battleground, with UAE and Bahrain well results due in 2H26.

Renewables and EPC previews from research: SHLS Overweight with Dec 2026 price target raised to $13 from $10 on expected share gains after a favorable ITC ruling. PRIM Energy segment had about $2.0bn in 2Q awards and a funnel above $7bn, with a 2H26 renewables bookings target of about $2bn. RUN watched for demand updates, project monetization and the Tesla and Renew distributed power program.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised to $13 from $10 on a higher multiple. JPM expects market share gains from 2H26 after an ITC ruling blocked its largest competitor's core product imports.
Setup is constructive, with about $2.0bn in 2Q Energy awards led by gas generation and a funnel above $7bn. The stock should react well if renewables show no further deterioration.
Upbeat print expected on productivity trends. A power project FID is possible in 2026 or early 2027, though details are unlikely until the decision is firm.
JPM's Arun Jayaram expects a medium-term growth outlook through 2029 that could quantify free cash flow growth and act as a mini-catalyst. Bears say it is already well telegraphed.

Seen as a hedge fund short because catalysts are far out and the capex drop-off may be less sharp than implied. JPM expects a favorable Willow resource update without a sustained step-up in Alaska capex.
Bulls look for UAE and Bahrain well results and productivity stabilization. Bears say these are already priced in after recent outperformance.
Described as a tricky setup: possibly the most crowded long in midstream, with expectations for a power announcement that some investors doubt is coming.

sector_views.rationale: The author argues resource equities benefit if 2026 resembles 1965 without commodity price controls, and questions current S&P 500 Energy and Materials weights.
Demand is strong but multiples are exposed to a higher discount rate as long yields rise.
Mixed positioning: WMB, KGS and ET crowded longs, OKE the crowded short, PAA near neutral.
Sentiment improving and stocks seen as cheap, but no meaningful deal updates are expected.

earnings_insights: MTZ 2Q26: backlog hit a record of about $7.8bn with a book-to-bill of 1.3x. Renewables backlog has grown sequentially for 12 consecutive quarters. Management called data center demand 'absolutely unreal' (reported 2Q26 call).
NUE 2Q26 call: record or near-record backlogs and order entry rates across product groups, and management says demand rather than price is driving results (reported).
FCX 2Q26 call: customers report robust copper demand tied to AI data centers and energy infrastructure, with improved auto demand more than offsetting weak private construction (reported).
GEV 2Q26 call: management is comfortable with supply relative to demand over the next five to six years, and expects 30 GW of outage-related capacity deliverable in 2030 and 2031 (reported).
Upcoming 2Q26 reports (week of 3 Aug 2026): FANG on Monday, then DVN, OXY, COP, EOG, WMB, PAA, KGS, TRGP, SHLS, PRIM, RUN. These are previews of upcoming prints, not results.
KGS: Eli Jossen expects 2Q power infrastructure capex above the $400-500mm 2026 guide (JPM estimate, upcoming print).
DVN: Arun Jayaram sees low risk of a negative surprise because the company had visibility on about 75% of the quarter when it issued its updated 2Q26 outlook (JPM preview).
COP: Arun Jayaram expects a favorable Willow resource update that could exceed the initial 600 million barrel case (JPM preview, upcoming print).

risk_factors: Inflation right-tail risk: CPI used to justify staying on hold may be out of touch with what is coming, as in 1965.
Rising long-end yields compress equity multiples even when demand and earnings are strong.
The commodity price controls that buffered inflation in the 1960s do not exist today.
Behind-the-meter power names face crowded positioning and the risk of a poor reception to earnings.
SOBO's Bridger pipeline faces a regulatory setback after Montana's environmental agency rescinded a waiver, which investors compare with the Keystone XL episode.
Renewables portfolio deterioration at PRIM and lumpy BESS order activity at SHLS.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand for power, steel, copper and refined products is strong, and hyperscaler capex rose with some signs of improving ROIC, which equity investors expected to support momentum and power stocks.
tension_points.bear_case: The bond market is pricing a hotter inflation path with a soft Fed. A higher discount rate compresses multiples even when demand is strong, as in 2022 and 1965-67.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Long-end yields stabilizing or falling. The author's own framing is that the 30-year rise of 11bps on the Fed decision day signals the bond market pushing back.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM's Arun Jayaram expects OXY to lay out building blocks for free cash flow growth through 2029 and possibly quantify it, a mini-catalyst.
tension_points.bear_case: Bears say the cash flow update is well telegraphed and should not be rewarded yet, like COP's distant cash flow inflection.

tension_points.bull_case: Bulls look for a positive UAE and Bahrain well results update and further stabilization in productivity trends.
tension_points.bear_case: Bears say this is already in the recent outperformance versus peers, and the UAE production sharing agreement terms are not yet known.
